summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR 1,441 crore with EBITDA margin at 15.1%; FY26 order inflow up 109% to INR 7,687 crore.
summary.overview: STL reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 1,441 crore (+37% YoY) and EBITDA margin of 15.1%, with PAT turning positive in the quarter and for the full year. FY26 revenue was INR 4,745 crore and EBITDA INR 628 crore (+39%, margin 13.2%). Order inflow more than doubled and the open order book rose 67% to INR 7,309 crore, though management said raw material availability (germanium, helium, polymers) remains constrained and costs are rising due to the West Asia conflict. Management reiterated a 20% reported EBITDA margin target by end of FY27 and a rise in Enterprise and Data Center share of revenue to 30%.

segments.name: Telecom and Citizen Networks
segments.commentary: Described as the core contributor to revenue; no separate figures disclosed in the call.

segments.name: Enterprise and Data Center
segments.commentary: Share of revenue moderated to 19% in FY26, mainly due to lower copper business on higher LME prices; management targets 30% of revenue in the current fiscal. Data center revenue not broken out.

segments.name: North America / Europe
segments.commentary: North America share of revenue rose from 25% in FY25 to 39% in FY26; Europe remains a significant contributor at 40%.

segments.name: STL Digital (IT services)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 284 crore (vs INR 290 crore), EBITDA INR 3 crore; nine new customer logos added, total 35 customers.

guidance_outlook: Structural EBITDA margin on track for 20% at reported level by end of FY27 (Q4 FY27), per CFO; this was brought forward and kept at current tariff rates.
Enterprise and Data Center to scale to 30% of revenues in the current fiscal (FY27), brought forward from earlier 12-18 month timeline per analyst.

Q1 FY27: tariff impact positive as US tariffs fell from 50% to 15%, with US revenue expected to rise; offset by higher input costs from West Asia war. Margin expected to improve from Q4 levels but no numeric guidance given.
Raw material constraints (germanium, helium) expected to ease quarter-on-quarter; management said some volume is secured for rest of year.
Net debt/EBITDA target revised to below 1.2x from earlier 2x ceiling.
Management declined to provide FY27 revenue or margin growth guidance beyond the above.
capex_capacity: Near-term capex of approximately INR 500 crore planned for technology leadership and upgrading asset base to support high-value data center portfolio offerings.
Management declined to disclose IBR capacity, preform sourcing mix, or post-capex OFC capacity; said capacities will no longer be disclosed.
Management declined to comment on timing of IBR line upgrade (analyst cited June 2026 target).
Current utilisation improved slightly QoQ; management would not give a number, citing raw material constraints.
demand_pricing: Company does not sell in the spot market; focus on long-term contracts with customers in Europe, US and India.
Global optical cable demand growth for 2026 upgraded to about 6.8% YoY (CRU); North America expected to be strongest region with 15% CAGR to 2030.
Global ex-China OFC market share stable at around 8% in FY26 despite US tariff and germanium constraints.
Optical connectivity attach rate moderated to 15% in FY26 from 22% in FY25, attributed to product mix, project timing and a higher OFC revenue base; management says it is temporary.
Data center margin profile described as better than telecom; more sales to move to end-to-end solutions.
Management said it is actively supplying into the hyperscaler market and is in long-term partnership discussions, without naming deals.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation levels and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give a figure; utilisation improved slightly, and raw material constraints are expected to ease QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Recent QIP approval and capital needs?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the fundraise resolution is an annual enabling resolution; near-term capex of about INR 500 crore for data center upgrades is identified.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory with US tariffs falling from 50% to 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 gets a tariff tailwind and higher US revenue, offset by rising input costs from the war; margins expected to improve from Q4 without quantification.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 30% enterprise/data center target and 20% margin target brought forward?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO linked margin expansion to data center mix and said the 20% target by end-Q4 is achievable with correct execution at current tariffs.

qa_highlights.question: Amount of US tariffs paid and refund process?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said tariffs paid are north of INR 100 crore; refund process has started in the US but no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Prysmian litigation status?
qa_highlights.answer: Appeal filed September 2025 and pending before a three-judge bench; two further appeal stages remain (full bench, Supreme Court).

risks_watch: Germanium, helium and polymer availability and cost; management says availability is the bigger issue.
Margin offset from West Asia-driven input cost increases versus tariff benefit.
Data center and hyperscaler contract wins: no named multi-year capacity deals; analysts questioned slow volume pickup versus peers.
Attach rate fell to 15% from 22%; management says recovery timing is hard to predict.
Prysmian litigation (reported liability around USD 100 million per analyst) still in appeal.
Timing and amount of US tariff refunds not yet defined.
Management declined to disclose key operating metrics (capacity, preform sourcing, IBR capacity), limiting analysis.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and long-term data center opportunity, but guarded on specifics: repeatedly declined to disclose capacity, utilisation, customer names, hyperscaler timelines and refund amounts. Cautious on near-term costs, with input availability described as the key constraint.
key_quotes: We do not play in the spot market and we do not sell in the spot market.
The moderation is temporary and the long-term opportunity of connectivity remains very strong.
So we do target to have it by the end of Q4, the margins which I have mentioned.

financial_highlights.change: Expanded; company cites scale and product mix
+67% YoY (FY25: INR 4,378 crore); INR 1,468 crore slated for Q1 FY27

adds.what: Near-term technology leadership and asset base upgrade for data center portfolio (INR ~500 crore capex; no specific capacity figure disclosed)

growth.why: Management guides to 20% reported EBITDA margin by Q4 FY27 and Enterprise/Data Center scaling to 30% of revenue in FY27, backed by a FY26 order book of INR 7,309 crore (+67% YoY, INR 1,468 crore slated for Q1 FY27) and ~INR 500 crore upgrade capex, but no revenue growth guidance was given and capacity figures were not disclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: Q1 FY27 onward; 20% reported EBITDA by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management reiterated 20% reported EBITDA margin by end FY27 (vs 15.1% in Q4 FY26 and 13.2% in FY26), tied to data center mix and a US tariff cut from 50% to 15%, though West Asia input costs offset part of it and no quarterly number was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Near-term capex of about INR 500 crore is for technology leadership and asset base upgrades, not explicitly new capacity, and management declined to disclose IBR or OFC capacity or the timing of the IBR line upgrade (analyst cited June 2026).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Open order book rose 67% to INR 7,309 crore with INR 1,468 crore slated for Q1 FY27, and US revenue is expected to rise after tariffs fell to 15%, though raw material constraints (germanium, helium) cap output and utilisation was not quantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management has identified about INR 500 crore of near-term capex for data center upgrades and set a net debt/EBITDA ceiling below 1.2x; utilisation is undisclosed but described as only slightly improved, so the capex is being planned rather than forced by capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Enterprise/data center share target was pulled forward to 30% in FY27 from a 12-18 month timeline, but management gave no revenue or margin growth guidance and the input cost headwind is still open.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material shortages (germanium, helium, polymers) and West Asia-driven cost increases could offset the tariff tailwind, and the attach rate fell to 15% from 22%.

rows.label: US tariff reduction and refund
rows.why: US tariffs fell from 50% to 15%, a Q1 FY27 tailwind, and tariffs paid exceed INR 100 crore with refunds started in the US but no timeline given.

rows.label: Order book conversion into Q1 FY27
rows.why: INR 1,468 crore of the INR 7,309 crore open order book is slated for Q1 FY27, against FY26 order inflow of INR 7,687 crore (+109% YoY).

rows.label: Prysmian litigation appeal
rows.why: Appeal filed September 2025 is pending before a three-judge bench with two more appeal stages; analysts cite a reported liability of around USD 100 million.

tone.note: Management was confident on the data center opportunity, the 20% margin target and the 30% enterprise share, but declined to disclose capacity, utilisation, hyperscaler timelines and refund amounts; analysts pressed on slow volume pickup versus peers, the IBR upgrade timing and the attach rate drop
